first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and may also help recover activation, with two inherited findings indicating improved time-to-value and durable first-week activation. Promotional pricing could counter the competitor but carries documented 30-day retention harm, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the two most relevant onboarding records before final commitment, while retaining uncertainty about downstream retention and revenue impact.

final.rationale: Run a standard controlled onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified evidence directly matches both current declines: shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Measure qualified revenue and retention as guardrails because the SMB result included a 1% retention decline and has not generalized beyond SMB. Avoid promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence shows material retention harm.
